pll1d37c6-d1e3501.summary: Two senses of local or circumscribable: having dimension producing distance in place, and being defined by place (here and not everywhere), the latter applicable to every created spirit.
claims: 'Local' has two senses: dimensional and definitional.
Every created spirit is local in the definitional sense.

pll1d37c6-d1e3504.summary: Applies: bodies are local in every way; created spirits are local by definition of place but not dimensionally.
claims: Created spirits are local only by place-definition, not by dimension.

pll1d37c6-d1e3507.summary: Only the divine essence is wholly non-local and uncircumscribed, moved neither by place nor by time (affection and cognition); change by these two modes belongs to creatures.
claims: God alone is wholly non-local and uncircumscribed.
Change by place and time belongs to creatures, not God.

pll1d37c6-d1e3511.summary: Augustine, De Genesi ad litteram: God moves spiritual creatures through time and bodies through time and place while remaining unchanged, being interior to and exterior to all things, prior to and posterior to all.
claims: God moves creatures through time and place while his own substance remains immutable.
God is interior, exterior, prior, and later than all things.

pll1d37c6-d1e3533.summary: Conclusion from Augustine: God is not changed or moved by place or time; spiritual creatures move through time, bodily through time and place.
claims: God is not moved by place or time.
Spiritual creatures move by time, bodily by time and place.

pl-l1d37c6.summary: Distinguishes two senses of 'local' or 'circumscribed' (having dimension; being defined by place so as not to be everywhere): bodies are local in both, created spirits in the second only, God in neither. Confirms by Augustine that God moves creatures through time and place without himself changing.
claims: Bodies are local in both senses; created spirits only in the second; God in neither.
Creatures change by time and place; God does neither.
Spiritual creatures move by time, bodily creatures by time and place.
